items.meaning: Feed-mode assignment matches on the documented Fanuc-style and Haas lathes.
items.notes: Both use G98 = feed per MINUTE and G99 = feed per REVOLUTION in the lathe context documented here. Mill meanings differ, and control options can vary, so verify the exact machine manual before porting code.

items.meaning: Inch vs metric input — same on both, but confirm Setting 9 on Haas.
items.notes: Both brands use G20=inch, G21=metric. On Haas, G20/G21 check Setting 9 (Inch/Metric) rather than converting stored coordinates; other controls may differ. Verify the active unit mode, don't assume.

On Fanuc-style lathes G50 commonly clamps maximum spindle RPM (used with G96 constant surface speed). On some other controls G50 sets the coordinate system. Never assume — verify the machine manual before using G50.

items.meaning: Canned-cycle PARAMETER FORMAT varies by control generation.
items.notes: The letter order and whether the cycle is one-line or two-line differs between Fanuc generations and other brands (incl. Haas). Copying a cycle block verbatim across brands will likely be misread. Match the exact format in your control's programming manual.

items.meaning: Gear-range and chuck codes are BUILDER-DEFINED, not universal.
items.notes: M41/M42 (gear range) and M23/M24 (chuck open/close) exist on some machines but are NOT standard Fanuc codes — they are set by the machine builder (e.g. your Johnford HT 60CX-2D). Do not assume these work; check the builder's manual. M00–M30 are the near-universal set.

items.meaning: Verify against YOUR machine's manual — not a generic list.
items.notes: Fanuc publishes per-model manuals (e.g. 0i-T, 18i-T); Haas publishes per-model code pages. Builder options, parameter settings, and ladder logic remap codes. The lists here are a learning aid — the machine manual and a dry run / single-block prove-out are the real authority.
